data.title: Chinese students ripped off by condo agents
data.description: A group of Chinese students on Tuesday filed a police complaint against a condominium agent they had paid about 10 million baht to arrange rented accommodation, but had failed to do so.

data.title: Bangkok council seeks cable solutions
data.description: Bangkok councillors have approved a special committee to study solutions for disorganised communication cables, including relocating them underground on suitable roads, with a 90-day deadline for its review.

data.title: City Hall extends flood aid registration period as delays mount
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has extended the deadline for flood victims to file the paperwork needed for financial assistance for another month, until the end of November.

data.title: Five tonnes of cannabis buds seized in Bangkok
data.description: Police have arrested four Myanmar workers and their Vietnamese boss and seized five tonnes of cannabis buds at a rented house in Bangkok, and caught five Thais on a central plains highway with 284 kilogrammes of crystal meth.

data.title: Heroin bound for Australia seized
data.description: SAMUT PRAKAN: Narcotics officers have seized about 7kg of heroin concealed in instant-drink sachets in two parcels destined for Australia.

data.title: Council seeks cable solutions
data.description: Bangkok councillors have approved a special committee to study solutions for disorganised communication cables, including relocating them underground on suitable roads, with a 90-day deadline for its review.

data.title: Virgin Atlantic lands in Phuket
data.description: Thailand welcomed Virgin Atlantic's inaugural direct flight from London Heathrow to Phuket on Monday, as advance bookings from the UK rose 17.5% ahead of the high season.

data.title: New pilot zone to curb bribery
data.description: The government will use Bangkok's Khao San Road as a pilot zone to tackle bribery involving entertainment venues and speed up action against corrupt officials.

data.title: Group calls for halt to social security advisers' selection
data.description: The Progressive Social Security group has called for a halt to the selection of advisers to the Social Security Board, saying the selection committee must be named by the newly elected board.

data.title: House re-invites MP Suchada to explain gambling claims
data.description: A House committee will again invite Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap and her husband to explain alleged links to online gambling and a reported bribery offer at its meeting on Thursday, chairman Rangsiman Rome said on Monday.

data.title: Deadlock over debate time persists
data.description: The government and opposition remain at odds over the duration of the upcoming no-confidence debate, with the government proposing three days and the opposition holding firm on its demand for five.

data.title: Orange Line trials to start late next year
data.description: The eastern section of the Orange Line MRT is slated to open for trial runs starting from December next year, with fare collection set to begin in January the following year.

data.title: New Cold War tests Thai choices
data.description: A new Cold War is emerging as the United States and China compete from trade and finance to outer space, scholars and senior journalists have warned, urging Thailand not to pick sides too soon.

data.title: Minister orders checks over pollution complaints
data.description: Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa on Monday ordered further factory inspections and water sampling in Prachin Buri after residents complained of pollution, pledging that any action would comply with the law.

data.title: Digital wallets lead to Cambodia scam
data.description: Police traced cryptocurrency transactions across dozens of anonymous digital wallets to identify a money-laundering network linked to scam operations in Cambodia, leading to 39 arrests and the seizure of assets worth more than 500 million baht.

data.title: NSC steps up southern safeguards
data.description: The National Security Council (NSC) is stepping up preventive measures in the southern border provinces alongside peace talks, seeking to prevent further incidents and rebuild public trust.

data.title: BMA apologises for flood relief delays
data.description: Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt has apologised to flood-hit residents after applications for financial assistance surged beyond expectations, with more than 1 million claims registered.

data.title: Govt 'committed' to protecting territory
data.description: Thailand has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting its sovereignty in maritime boundary talks with Cambodia, as the two countries consider measures to ease tensions and keep negotiations on track.

data.title: New travel  subsidies for tour groups
data.description: The government is offering transport subsidies of up to 40,000 baht per trip to encourage domestic group travel and generate at least 208.8 million baht in tourism revenue.

data.title: Zoo turns viral hippo feeding fail into visitor attraction
data.description: A Thai zoo has responded to a viral video showing a woman repeatedly trying and failing to feed a hippopotamus by introducing a hippo statue that allows visitors to practice their aim, turning an internet sensation into an interactive attraction.

data.title: Lampang school hit by second fire in three days
data.description: LAMPANG — About 40 students fled a classroom at Bunyawat Witthayalai School on Monday after an air conditioner caught fire, the second blaze at the school in three days. No injuries were reported.

data.title: Kaeng Krachan race route revised over environmental concerns
data.description: Organisers of the Kaeng Krachan trail race have agreed to revise the route following opposition from environmental groups and academics concerned about the impact on the national park's fragile ecosystem.

data.title: Thai, S. Korean police bust scam centres in Bangkok
data.description: Thai and South Korean police have arrested two Chinese nationals and eight South Koreans suspected of operating three call scam centres in Bangkok that allegedly defrauded South Korean victims of more than 100 million baht.

data.title: PM orders nationwide review of illegal foreign land ownership by end of December
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered provincial governors to look into land plots suspected of being illegally owned by foreigners by the end of December, with a view to subsequently revoking the title deeds.

data.title: New dinosaur tracks find in Udon Thani
data.description: What are believed to be fossilised dinosaur footprints have been discovered in Ban Phue district of Udon Thani province, with preliminary observations suggesting they were left by a large carnivore.

data.title: S.Korean factory owner jailed for anal assault on Thai worker
data.description: A South Korean factory owner who injured an illegal Thai worker by inserting a compressed-air gun nozzle into his anus has been jailed for three years. A charge against his wife was dropped.

data.title: Flooding remains in Bangkok and 22 provinces
data.description: Flooding continues in parts of Bangkok and 22 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were falling on Monday, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation.

data.title: China’s embassy issues fresh Thailand travel alert over kidnappings, job scams
data.description: China's embassy in Thailand has warned citizens to carefully plan their trips and pay extra attention to transport security following a string of high-profile kidnappings targeting Chinese nationals.

data.title: Rail travel to expand in 5 provinces
data.description: The Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) plans to expand rail-based public transport into five regional provinces, aiming to improve connectivity, attract investment and support economic growth beyond Bangkok.

data.title: Ministry eyes extension to B40 promotion train tickets
data.description: The Transport Ministry is considering extending the 40-baht all-day fare scheme for Bangkok's Red and Purple electric train lines beyond its Nov 30 expiry.

data.title: Dept opposes plan to open mine near world heritage site
data.description: A conservation agency in Phetchaburi has opposed a proposed dolomite mine near Kaeng Krachan World Heritage Site, warning of potential harm to wildlife, water resources and local communities.

data.title: Dolphin conservation efforts broaden
data.description: On the shores of Songkhla Lake, the survival of endangered Irrawaddy dolphins is tied to the livelihoods of the people who share their habitat.

data.title: Probe into brazen Korat encroachment steps up
data.description: A probe into the encroachment of more than 189 rai (about 75 acres) of national forest reserves in Nakhon Ratchasima will accelerate after surveys confirmed it was all protected land.

data.title: Nida poll: Interior Ministry seen facing toughest censure grilling
data.description: The Interior Ministry is expected to face the toughest scrutiny in the coming no-confidence debate, according to a Nida Poll survey, with 45% of the respondents believing the opposition has solid evidence against the 18 targeted cabinet ministers.

data.title: Prachin Buri oil leak suspected
data.description: The Pollution Control Department (PCD) is now testing water quality and preparing to contain oil slicks in Prachin Buri after a suspected oil film was detected, amid concerns it could reach the Prachin Buri River.

data.title: Online gambling crackdown  deemed 'ineffective' by ex-MP
data.description: Former Democrat Party MP Sirichoke Sopha has questioned the effectiveness of the Digital Economy and Society (DES) Ministry's crackdown on online gambling, claiming that five major betting websites remain accessible from Thailand despite the ministry's announcement that it had blocked 945,075 links.
